added.title: Intermediate Permitting Specialist - Environmental Scientist
added.description:
Intermediate Permitting Specialist

Play an integral role in Worley Consulting’s Environmental & Sustainability (E&S) team, helping energy sector clients navigate environmental permitting and regulatory requirements while supporting the responsible development and delivery of complex projects across the United States.

You will work alongside experienced environmental practitioners, engineers and project professionals on projects spanning upstream, midstream and downstream energy, as well as emerging markets such as hydrogen, carbon capture, renewable power and biofuels. This is an opportunity to strengthen your technical expertise, gain meaningful client and regulatory exposure, and build your consulting career within a collaborative global organization.

Purpose of the role

As an Intermediate Permitting Specialist, you will support the planning, preparation and delivery of environmental permitting and regulatory solutions for energy and infrastructure projects.

You will help identify permitting requirements, prepare applications and technical documentation, maintain permit schedules and compliance requirements, and support engagement with clients, regulatory agencies and other stakeholders. Working with senior consultants and technical specialists, you will develop practical regulatory strategies that align environmental requirements with project objectives, schedules and delivery priorities.

The role offers a strong development pathway for an environmental professional who wants to deepen their permitting expertise, expand their client-facing capabilities and contribute to Worley Consulting’s continued growth in established and emerging energy markets.

Location(s)

This is a full-time, hybrid position based near a Worley U.S. office.

Desired locations: Houston TX, Long Beach or Monrovia CA, Chicago IL, Charleston WV, or Reading PA.

You will be collaborating with colleagues, clients and project teams across multiple locations. Travel to client meetings, regulatory engagements and project or field locations will be required based on project needs.

You Will Be Responsible For

Support environmental permitting, regulatory and advisory services for energy and infrastructure projects.
Identify federal, state and local permitting requirements and help develop strategies aligned with project objectives and schedules.
Prepare compliant permit applications, supporting technical studies, regulatory documentation and approval packages.
Support environmental permitting and reviews under NEPA, CEQA and other applicable federal, state and local frameworks.
Develop and maintain permit matrices, tracking tools, schedules and compliance databases to track regulatory milestones, permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
Prepare and review accurate, high-quality technical correspondence, environmental reports, work plans, project documentation, cost estimates and schedules.
Collaborate with senior environmental professionals, engineers and project teams to integrate permitting into multidisciplinary project planning and execution.
Engage with regulators, clients and project stakeholders, developing communication and consulting skills to support successful project outcomes.
Support project management by coordinating assigned tasks and tracking scope, schedule, budget and progress.
Support proposals, scope development, cost estimates and opportunity identification.
Support quality assurance and alignment with Worley’s E&S systems, technical standards and HSE expectations.
Participate in client meetings and field programs, traveling as needed for effective project delivery.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

You will bring a foundation in environmental permitting or regulatory consulting combined with strong technical writing, analytical and collaboration skills. You will be motivated to expand your expertise and take on increasing responsibility as part of multidisciplinary project teams.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Biology or a related discipline.
Typically 3–7 years of relevant experience, preferably in environmental consulting, engineering or regulation.
Working knowledge of U.S. environmental permitting, including NEPA and applicable federal and state requirements.
Familiarity with federal regulations, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act.
Understanding of environmental compliance and permitting, including air and/or water requirements.
Experience supporting environmental permitting and preparing accurate, organized technical and regulatory documentation.
Demonstrated ability to track assigned project scope, schedules and budgets and identify potential variances.
Strong technical writing, reporting and documentation skills focused on quality, accuracy and detail.
Developing client-facing and stakeholder engagement skills; effective communication with clients, regulators and project teams.
Strong communication and collaboration skills for effective multidisciplinary teamwork.
Commitment to health, safety, environmental stewardship and responsible project delivery.
Motivation to build technical and consulting skills with guidance from experienced practitioners.

Additional Preferred Experience

Air quality permitting support experience and exposure to emissions modeling or regulatory strategy development.
Familiarity with CEQA and California environmental permitting requirements.
Exposure to environmental engineering, including stormwater management and Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) planning.
Experience supporting proposals, cost estimates or project planning.
Experience or demonstrated interest in emerging energy sectors, including hydrogen, carbon capture and management, renewable power and biofuels.

Compensation

For California applicants

Salary Range: $85,398 - $113,821; based upon experience
Benefits: eligible for PTO, 401k, medical, vision, dental, etc.

Los Angeles

We will consider for employment all qualified Applicants, including those with Criminal Histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles' Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

Application of the pay band: Variation in salary is determined by factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, relevant years of experience, geographic location, internal pay equity, and prevailing market conditions for the specific role.

Benefits

Feel the energy at Worley with access to a range of benefits including paid time off, holiday pay (usually 8 per year in the US), and eligibility to participate in the medical, life, dental, and vision insurance plans, as well as 401K plan.

Apply today

Bring your environmental permitting experience, curiosity and collaborative approach to a role where you can contribute to meaningful projects while continuing to develop as a trusted environmental professional.

You will have the opportunity to learn from experienced practitioners, work across multidisciplinary teams, gain exposure to clients and regulators, and broaden your experience across established and emerging energy markets. As your expertise develops, you will have opportunities to take on greater technical, project delivery and client responsibilities.

About Us

Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today’s needs and transition to more sustainable solutions. Join us and help drive innovation and sustainability in our projects.

Moving forward together

We want our people to be energized and empowered to drive sustainable impact. So, our focus is on a values-inspired culture that unlocks brilliance through belonging, connection and innovation. We’re building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Creating a space where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and are heard.

And we’re not just talking about it; we’re doing it. We’re reskilling our people, leveraging transferable skills, and supporting the transition of our workforce to become experts in today’s low carbon energy infrastructure and technology. Whatever your ambition, there’s a path for you here. And there’s no barrier to your potential career success. Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities, and be part of delivering sustainable change.

added.title: Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty in Environmental Health
added.description:
Description

Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty in Environmental Health

Rice University invites applications for multiple tenured and tenure-track positions at the senior and junior levels in Environmental Health, with preferred focus areas in environmental and occupational epidemiology, environmental exposures and sustainability, environmental risk assessment, toxicology, infectious diseases, global environmental health, and climate impacts on health, as well as the intersection of these areas with environmental justice. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027. The ideal candidate(s) would bring an interdisciplinary approach, leveraging quantitative training in biostatistics, epidemiological modeling, spatial analytics (GIS), or AI/data science, with experience analyzing clinical (e.g., electronic medical records), registry (e.g., Texas Cancer Registry), or administrative (e.g., American Community Survey) health data.

Primary academic appointment will be in the Department of Kinesiology, ranked #1 nationally by the popular Niche™ rankings and home to Rice’s Public Health Sciences and Sports Medicine and Exercise Physiology undergraduate degrees. These positions are part of an initiative to support interdisciplinary environmental health scholarship, including a new Climate + Health Excellence Center ( FORECAST ) funded by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund. They will come with robust joint appointments in Departments of BioSciences, Chemistry, and Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences as most appropriate.

The successful candidate(s) will be expected to establish a vibrant, externally funded research program, collaborate across disciplines, and teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels. We especially encourage applications from scientists addressing climate impacts on human health and infectious disease, and contributing to broad themes of sustainability or One Health principles. Potential to connect to exercise science, the department’s other major intellectual theme, will also be explored, such as through interests in impacts of extreme heat, air quality, and toxicants on human physiology and performance.

Candidates must have a PhD, DrPH, or equivalent degree in public health science or a relevant field of natural science or engineering and have completed the requirements for the degree by July 1, 2027.

To apply, please submit the following materials online at https://apply.interfolio.com/193813 : (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) research statement (3 pages max); (4) statement of teaching philosophy (3 pages max); and (5) contact information for three references. The research statement and statement of teaching philosophy may also include plans for building a diverse and inclusive research group and fostering equitable and inclusive classrooms. Applications that are received by November 16, 2026,
will receive full consideration, but we will continue reviewing applications until positions are filled. For additional information, please visit our department website or contact the search chairs, Dr. Cassandra Diep ( csdiep@rice.edu ) and Dr. Scott P. Egan ( scott.p.egan@rice.edu) .

Rice University is located in Houston, Texas, USA, and is a private, coeducational, nonsectarian university that aspires to path-breaking research, unsurpassed teaching, and contributions to the betterment of our world. Rice fulfills this mission by cultivating a diverse community of learning and discovery that produces leaders across the spectrum of human endeavor. In our candidate pools, we seek to attract greater representation of women, scholars of color, people with disabilities, veterans, and others who have historically been underrepresented in academia; accelerate progress in building a faculty and staff varied in background and thought; and maintain an environment that fosters interaction and understanding within our community.

Application Instructions

Rice University
is an Equal Opportunity Employer with commitment to diversity at all levels, and considers for employment qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, genetic information, disability or protected veteran status.

Company Overview

EKI Environment & Water, Inc. (EKI) is an employee-owned engineering, environmental, and water resources consulting firm serving private- and public-sector clients throughout the United States. The Water Resources Principal Hydrogeologist reports to the Regional Director (RD) and is responsible for leading and executing hydrogeologic consulting services in the Colorado and Rocky Mountain growth areas while supporting EKI’s business in other geographies such as California, Washington, Texas, and New England. The Principal Hydrogeologist will manage technical projects, grow and lead a team of hydrogeologist and groundwater modelers, provide technical leadership within the Colorado water resource professional community, grow technical capabilities across the organization, lead strategic initiatives, encourage risk stewardship, and develop business and client relationships. Projects may include groundwater management assistance, water rights engineering, groundwater basin characterization, groundwater modeling, water supply planning and development, reuse planning, litigation support, managed aquifer recharge, and more.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Responsibilities may include, but will not be limited to the following:

Provide expertise, technical guidance, and oversight on water resources projects such as:
Hydrogeologic conceptual models, water balances, numerical model development, and groundwater sustainability plans
Colorado water rights engineering
Expert testimony and litigation support
Water supply assessments and water management plans
Water supply strategies and integrated plans; and/or
Groundwater well design, construction, and testing

Maintain awareness of technical innovations, new industry developments and standards, and identify opportunities to pursue, with a focus on Colorado
Design, develop, and implement quality assurance/quality control protocols for projects and proposals
Provide external leadership and support regional presence in professional groups and forums, including leading and participating in client meetings, conferences, industry associations, and/or technical committees
Provide internal leadership strengthening EKI’s technical capabilities across the organization and mentoring early to mid-career professionals
Participate in strategic plan development and implementation
Identify hiring and training needs and support the hiring processes
Support professional development of team members to provide growth opportunities and expand technical capabilities, innovation, and expertise
Other duties as required

Qualifications & Requirements

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Hydrogeology, Geology, Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Hydrology, Earth Sciences, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Fifteen or more (15+) years of experience as a hydrogeologist working on water resources projects, experience in Colorado and the Rocky Mountain West preferred
Registration or licensure as a professional engineer or geoscientist preferred
Excellent client management skills with a proven ability to maintain long-term client relationships
Proven track record of executing contracts and developing ongoing and/or expanded services for clients
Knowledge of and experience with Colorado water rights, planning, management, and development

Competencies

Must have effective verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate and coordinate effectively with clients, subconsultants, regulatory agencies, and members of the public
Must have ability to conduct work in a manner consistent with EKI’s values – Integrated Solutions, Responsiveness, Ingenuity, Quality, Results
Must have a current valid driver’s license

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment with high-volume workload and frequent short deadlines
Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs
Must be able to work remaining in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods
Must be able to communicate with others to exchange information
Must be able to assess the accuracy, quality and thoroughness of the work assigned

Travel Requirements

Must be able to travel within Colorado and occasionally to other sites such as EKI offices, client offices, and project locations
Travel 25 to 40 percent of the time, occasionally overnight

SALARY RANGE

The expected base salary range for this position is $170,000 - $190,000 per year. Actual compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including the candidate's skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for an annual performance bonus based on individual and company performance.

As an employee-owned firm, EKI offers a unique company culture with a corporate commitment to maintaining a positive work/life experience. EKI provides excellent compensation and comprehensive benefits packages, including career advancement opportunities, outstanding training opportunities, incentive compensation including bonuses, retirement benefits and 401(k) profit-sharing contributions, and group medical, vision, and dental benefits.

EKI Environment & Water, Inc is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.

added.title: Principal, Air Quality Permitting and Compliance
added.description:
SLR combines strategic insight with practical technical expertise to address the challenges shaping the energy industry today. Our powerhouse team of environmental and advisory consultants has been at the forefront of helping oil and gas industry clients to comply with complex regulations, tackle environmental and social challenges, and meet stakeholder expectations since SLR’s inception more than 30 years ago. SLR services continuously evolve alongside issues of importance to the oil and gas Industry, and we are currently providing support to large multinational and smaller local companies to succeed throughout the energy transition. While our environmental support for traditional oil and gas services has grown, our focus on other energy forms and issues has evolved and now additionally includes liquefied natural gas. renewables, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, carbon capture/sequestration, and decarbonization.

SLR is a recognized leader in environmental consulting to the energy industry, which is our largest North American business sector. The SLR team in North America comprises more than 1500 scientists and engineers providing end-to-end services that drive value and minimize risk throughout the oil and gas value chain.

We are now looking for a Principal Consultant to help SLR further grow our oil and gas industry business in the Gulf Coast Region.

Role

As a Principal Consultant
, you will play a significant role in growing our Gulf Coast base of oil and gas clients and our team of air quality professionals in Texas and Louisiana. We will rely on you to help lead the expansion of our business in the largest oil and gas producing region in the U.S. You will lead consulting projects for key oil and gas clients, expand our oil and gas industry business, mentor rising talent, and foster a culture of growth and excellence.

The Ideal Candidate Will

Drive new client growth and expand consulting sales in the oil and gas sector Serve as a trusted advisor to industry clients, regulators, and stakeholders
Provide deep technical expertise in air quality permitting, compliance, and U.S. regulatory frameworks, including state requirements
Demonstrate subject matter leadership in air quality compliance solutions across upstream, midstream, and downstream operations
Build, manage, and grow strong client relationships, maintaining a diverse and active client portfolio
Lead business development efforts, including sales strategy, proposal development, and positioning of differentiated value
Leverage market intelligence and industry networks to identify opportunities and strengthen competitive positioning
Collaborate across teams to drive cross selling, share insights, and develop new services aligned to market needs
Lead major client projects to ensure successful delivery, deepen client understanding, and generate repeat work
Mentor staff and support development of marketing materials, thought leadership, and client communications

Responsibilities

Apply extensive environmental, regulatory, and technical knowledge of the oil and gas industry to design and deliver effective air quality permitting and compliance services to upstream, midstream, and downstream oil and gas clients.
Be client facing and leverage deep expertise in air quality permitting, and compliance to effectively advance client strategies and cultivate new client relationships.
Develop effective marketing strategies and sales tactics that lead to increased oil and gas business.
Cultivate long-term client satisfaction, retention, and loyalty.
Develop successful approaches to identify new opportunities and develop winning value propositions and proposals.
Provide clear, concise business-focused findings, recommendations, and options regarding client documentation.
Contribute to a high-performing team that works with a significant degree of collaboration and takes pride in the level and quality of service delivered to our clients. A highly positive, can-do attitude will help you thrive in this environment.
Develop, track, and document sales, project expectations, and budget.

Working @ SLR

Benefits

With us, there is no doubt you will grow your subject-matter expertise and oil and gas industry knowledge. We care about investing in our employees for the long run, and if you ask our team, they will tell you that is just one of the benefits of working here. We want to be a place where you can experience career growth and satisfaction now and in the future. Here is what else you will enjoy as part of our team:

Competitive total compensation package including medical, dental, orthodontia, vision, FSA/HSA, generous PTO accrual, ten paid holidays, 401(k) retirement account with company matching program, company paid life insurance, short- and long-term disability insurance, and employee assistance program.
The salary range for this position is $175,000 - $225,000. Final agreed upon compensation will be commensurate with individual education, professional designation, experience, internal parity, and location.
Full-time, permanent role with opportunities for professional growth and advancement.

Qualifications

Bachelor and/or Master of Science degree(s) in Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field
15-20 years’ experience in providing successful air quality consulting and/or in-house services to the oil and gas sector, including demonstrated success leading complex, multi-stakeholder projects.
Strong experience in consulting, client relationship management, and business development.
Strong knowledge of U.S. and state air quality regulations and permitting requirements applicable to the Gulf Coast oil and gas industry, with strong experience in regulatory applicability analysis and interpretation.
Established reputation in the oil and gas industry, with demonstrated credibility and visibility through regulatory engagement, client relationships, published work, conference participation, or industry association involvement.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and inspire technical teams.
Excellent communication and people skills, including negotiation, facilitation, and executive-level presentation.
Strong written communication skills for proposal/report writing, technical and marketing presentations, and peer review capabilities.
Professional Designation with appropriate Professional Organization.

DE&I are at the core of who we are and want to be. SLR is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity / Affirmative Action Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, civil union status, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or expression, genetic information, or veteran status.

We are committed to these values, and our SLR Culture & Diversity Team works to actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion across our people and talent processes, operations, and client work around the world.
